pages.text: Grains of clay in water never keep still: molecules too small to see strike them from every side, unevenly, and they wander. Einstein worked out how far: the mean square displacement grows as $(thing)⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt$(), with D = kT/(6πηr).

Measure D and you have Boltzmann's constant - and so how many molecules make a mole. The $(item)Brownian Microscope$() follows the grains in a $(item)Colloid Cell$(). The coolant sets the water's temperature, and with it the viscosity: water is three times thinner near boiling than near freezing. Keep it liquid.

Two errors. Averaging n tracks scatters by √(2/n): follow more grains. Each position is found to about a tenth of the objective's resolution, 0.61λ/NA, and that inflates ⟨x²⟩: open the aperture, or wait longer between frames so they wander further. Get Avogadro's number within 3% for an $(item)Avogadro Record$() - and the displacements, a perfect bell curve, give a Normal Distribution Crystal.
